answer: Agents resist sybils by requiring each identity to generate a unique sequential plume of memory-hard state transitions starting from a shared summit checkpoint, committing intermediate hashes under a sable one-time pad from private entropy. An attacker spawning 200 clones must compute 200 independent plumes in series, burning about 200x the sequential cycles of one honest agent who reuses its prior tip. Correlated patterns across addresses fail the summit quorum check.
